scores.notes: Closest to adventure.asia: full-bleed square-edged photo heroes on every page, Satisfy h2s, alternating cream/white/navy bands, uppercase place names, and the ribbon rebuilt properly. Its accessibility work is the most rigorous of the three. The scrim maths is correct: white text needs a scrim of at least .65, because .55 over (15,20,27) gives only about 4.2:1. Keyboard focus switches the ribbon to a scrollable still row, so a focused tile is never off-screen (WCAG 2.4.11). It adds a skip link and a native <dialog> mobile menu. The hero settle is at most 5 s and runs once, so it needs no pause control. Inter moves into app/plan/layout.tsx without restyling the planner. heroes.ts gives curated final CDN URLs and has a unit test. Weaknesses: (1) Every page leads with a big photo, including tour heroes that still go through the ~1.4 s 302. Only home and the 14 destinations are curated, and 8 of those have no cover. That gives the highest LCP risk. (2) The settle scales the LCP image itself. (3) The 96 px place name and 720-820 px heroes push the search card and CTA down. Conversion relies on a single search card. (4) The magazine grid needs strong unique covers, which the catalog does not have yet. (5) It uses --aa-band and --aa-on-band names that may collide with ADR 0016 core ownership.

The most conversion-minded and buildable of the three. It has one gold primary and one secondary CTA on every screen. The 'Ways in' trio reuses the brand icons. The navy CTA band has honest reassurances (no price or response-time claims). The tour page has a sticky aside at 1440 and a two-button sticky bar at 390. The featured carousel is user-driven with no autoplay and has proper carousel semantics. It has the best LCP plan for home: a static curated AVIF/WebP asset with an art-directed portrait crop, preload and fetchpriority. Destination and tour pages use a server-side resolvePhotoUrl() to skip the 302, and the plan rightly avoids next/image. Token hygiene is sound: B2C-only tokens use --tp-*, generic scales are offered to AA-994, and the muted fix to #5A6270 is backed by contrast numbers. Satisfy uses display: optional, so it causes no swap shift. Weaknesses: (1) The 16 s Ken Burns on the hero image goes against the plan's own 2.2.2 reasoning and animates the LCP image. Cap it at 5 s or drop it. (2) The scrim claim is wrong: .55 over (15,20,27) is about 4.3:1, not 4.7:1, so the bottom gradient must be at least .65 where text sits. (3) It has no mobile nav menu at 390 (links simply hidden). (4) The ribbon pauses on focus-within but stays clipped, so a focused tile can sit off-screen. (5) Switching the whole planner from Inter to Poppins in the same slice is risky (its own R10). (6) Four client islands give the most JS of the three, but it is still within the 5 KB budget.

The most distinctive direction and the most product-led. The plan card sits in the hero, the route draws in trip order, the map follows the day being read on the tour page, and the list highlights the matching map pin. The home LCP is the h1 text, which is the safest LCP choice of the three. It has excellent engineering details: the marquee duration is computed on the server (no JS measuring), a fill rule repeats items until the track is at least 2400 px wide, a CSS safety net covers reduced motion, a tokens.test.ts guard bans raw px/hex/duration values, theme switches suppress transitions so the page does not flash, and route and pin colours are checked for 3:1 non-text contrast. Weaknesses: (1) The home hero is a navy SVG map, not a photo. That departs from the adventure.asia look Nghiệp pointed to and from the research recommendation. (2) Feasibility this week is poor. It needs a Natural Earth → mapshaper generator, route projection, its own Mercator centre/zoom maths so an SVG layer lines up with the Mapbox static images (≤2 px), scroll-spy and pin drop-ins. That is many moving parts with a high chance of bugs. (3) It moves the AI pill off the header into the footer, which weakens the AA-805/AA-819 disclosure. Reject that. (4) There is the most self-moving motion on load (draw, pins, day steps, pin drops), which risks feeling busy for a brand whose own motion is restrained. (5) Destination and tour photo heroes still depend on the S0 photo URL fix.

graft:
Base: warm-clean ("Golden Hour"), with these grafts.

FROM IMMERSIVE:
1. Replace the 16 s Ken Burns with the immersive hero settle: scale 1.06→1, at most 4.8 s, once, CSS only, off under reduced motion. Or drop it on the LCP image entirely.
2. Use the immersive scrim rule. Hero and tile text sits where the scrim is at least .65 (.55 over (15,20,27) is only about 4.2–4.3:1). Add the white-on-scrim worst case to contrast.test.ts.
3. Ribbon still mode on keyboard focus: :has(:focus-visible) removes the animation and makes the track an overflow-x:auto snap row, so a focused tile scrolls into view (WCAG 2.4.11). This replaces "pause on focus-within" in a clipped track.
4. Add a 44 px menu button at 390 that opens a native <dialog> sheet (links + theme toggle, Esc closes it, focus returns to the button). Add a "Skip to content" link.
5. Add lib/heroes.ts, the curated map for the 14 destinations (final CDN src, srcSet, width, height, focal point, alt), with a unit test. Fallback order: catalog cover, then the navy typographic hero. This complements the static home asset and the server-side resolvePhotoUrl().
6. Move Inter into app/plan/layout.tsx for this slice. Do not switch the planner to Poppins yet; that waits for its own slice with 390 screenshots.
7. Destination hero name uses --aa-text-place (uppercase, tracked). No-photo tiles alternate navy and accent-tint, and two typographic tiles never sit next to each other.
8. Use content-visibility:auto plus contain-intrinsic-size on below-fold sections, keeping the first two sections and the #anchors off it.

FROM MAP-FIRST:
1. Compute the marquee duration on the server (--dur-sm and --dur-lg from n × (tile + gap) / speed, written inline). Add the fill rule: repeat inside copy A until it is at least 2400 px wide, with the repeats aria-hidden.
2. Add a mask-image edge fade (48 px) on the ribbon viewport.
3. In static mode at ≥768 px, show prev/next 44 px buttons.
4. Add the global @media (prefers-reduced-motion) safety net on top of the data-motion gate.
5. Add the theme-switch transition suppression (data-theme-switching for one frame).
6. Add lib/tokens.test.ts to ban text-[NNpx], raw hex and raw duration/ease values in app/ and components/site/.
7. Header shadow via scroll-driven CSS as a no-JS extra.
8. Later slices only: route and pin tokens (--aa-route, casing, pin) for /plan and the static maps, the place list ↔ map pin highlight, and the tour route scroll-spy. Do not graft the SVG Asia hero map or the Mercator overlay this week.

KEEP / REJECT:
- Keep the AI label chip in the header on every page; reject map-first moving it to the footer.
- Keep the ribbon as the only self-moving element.
- Raise two follow-up issues: a CIS issue for final CDN URLs plus a ~1000 w variant in the catalog contract, and a data issue for the missing country and tour covers.
